calls.thesis: Reiterated HOLD (prior HOLD 21 and 24 Oct): answering his own title question — sell or hold after a ~7-8% after-hours drop — he says Alphabet is not a stock he is going to be selling anytime soon. He argues the earnings miss is misunderstood: a one-time $8.7bn mark-to-market loss on equity positions (SpaceX, Anthropic) cut reported EPS to $2.12 vs ~$3 expected, while adjusted EPS is ~$2.67; revenue +25%, operating income +30%, Cloud +103% to $30.7bn at 36.2% margin, search still growing 12% with expanding margins. He holds Alphabet (position up ~100%) and calls the report reasonably good, while flagging two quarters of negative free cash flow (-$9bn this quarter) on $51bn quarterly capex and a 22x forward earnings multiple that is not the cheapest.
calls.price_at_call: Down ~7-8% after hours; ~22x forward earnings; $265bn cash vs $125bn debt

calls.thesis: First explicit Hogue BUY on Alphabet (prior tracked stance was UNCERTAIN): ahead of Wednesday earnings, revenue growth is forecast at 25% with earnings potentially reaching $15/share and revenue hitting ~$0.5 trillion this year, Bank of America sees a possible upside surprise (93% cloud growth and strong TPU sales), and the shares trade at ~20x this year's expected earnings versus ~30x in December. The key market risk he flags is capex guidance (expected ~$200bn this year, ~$300bn next, broadly unchanged).
calls.price_at_call: No share price stated; ~20x this year's expected earnings; analyst average target $430 (~33% upside), low $380 (~17%); his own view is back to about $400 over the next year

calls.thesis: Reiterated HOLD: he owns Alphabet, the only AI-related company in the Asymmetric Portfolio; hyperscalers like Alphabet will be fine because they have cash flow from core operations and can simply pull back capex spending if needed, unlike the capital-dependent neoclouds.

Owns Alphabet and thinks it will be just fine: hyperscalers have core businesses generating cash flow and can pull back capex if needed, unlike the capital-dependent neoclouds; he also owns companies using AI to improve physical-world products and efficiency.
New: "no way Jose" - search moat at risk, capex commitments make risk/reward unattractive.
calls.bull: AI monetization offsets search share loss.
